extracted.intended_audience: YouTube creators and digital marketers looking to optimize videos for platform ranking
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for creating and optimizing YouTube videos so they rank better across YouTube sections (Home, Recommended, Trending, Search, Subscriptions). Focuses on audience-first content, engagement metrics, keywords, and platform-specific behaviors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Algorithm goal — relevance and personalization
rubrics_metrics.description: YouTube’s algorithm aims to provide searchers with relevant, personalized videos across Home, Search, Recommended, Trending, and Subscriptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design videos to serve the interests of specific users rather than to 'beat the system.' The platform personalizes results per section to present options users will love.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audience-first content (don't game the system)
rubrics_metrics.description: YouTube wants videos that are created for your audience instead of trying to beat the system. You shouldn’t load your descriptions with keywords or create videos that you think the platform will like.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Create videos for your audience and your audience alone — this is enough to catch YouTube’s eye. Avoid keyword stuffing and irrelevant content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Home ranking — user watch history
rubrics_metrics.description: Home results focus solely on the users’ history: what they’ve watched before, whether they mostly listen to music, watch vlogs, and which channels they frequent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Produce content consistent with targeted viewers’ historic interests to increase chances of appearing on their Home screen.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommended ranking — collaborative/similarity factors
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommended results consider interaction between top videos and similar users: videos most-watched by similar audiences are ranked highly for users.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understand audience clusters (e.g., users who listen to the same band) and target content that performs well among those similar users to get recommended.

rubrics_metrics.name: Home/Recommended ranking — engagement/watch time
rubrics_metrics.description: YouTube suggests keeping users engaged for as long as possible to rank in the 'Home' section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Whether long or short videos, the goal is to keep people interested and engaged — higher total watch time and session duration improve chances of being featured on Home.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommended ranking — end-screen call-to-action
rubrics_metrics.description: To rank in the 'Recommended' section, YouTube suggests that the end screen of your videos close with a strong call to action that suggests your next video.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use end screens and CTAs that guide viewers to additional videos to increase internal navigation and recommendation signals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trending criteria — newness and country-specific popularity
rubrics_metrics.description: Trending pulls videos that are new and popular in a specific country; trending videos are never sponsored.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on recent, rapidly popular content within the target country; you cannot pay to appear in Trending.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trending criteria — growth rate and traffic sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Some trending placements are based on the rate of growth in views and where views are coming from.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rapid increases in views and diverse or organic traffic sources improve chances of trending; consider shareability and cross-platform distribution to accelerate growth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trending content quality — relatability and shareability
rubrics_metrics.description: YouTube suggests making videos that are widely relatable, broadly appealing, and easily shared to rank in Trending.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Create content with broad appeal and high share potential so it can reach audiences beyond your subscribers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Search ranking — relevance and keyword presence
rubrics_metrics.description: Search results are mostly based on the relevance of your video to the user’s search and whether the keyword (or variation) is present in your video’s title and/or description.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include search keywords in title and description and use tags to help rank; ensure content matches the search intent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Search optimization — extended descriptions and tag usage
rubrics_metrics.description: YouTube recommends writing extended descriptions that feature the keyword and using keywords in video tags to help rank for terms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write informative, relevant extended descriptions (without keyword stuffing) and use tags strategically to improve discoverability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Search anti-pattern — avoid keyword stuffing
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not keyword stuff or write content that isn’t relevant to your video.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keywords should be natural and directly relevant to video content; irrelevant or excessive keywords can harm rather than help ranking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subscriptions ranking — view velocity
rubrics_metrics.description: Subscriptions results ranking uses view velocity, which quantifies the number of subscribers that watch your video right after it’s published.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage subscribers to watch newly published videos quickly (e.g., through notifications, premieres) to raise view velocity and improve ranking on subscribers’ feeds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subscriptions ranking — subscriber count
rubrics_metrics.description: YouTube also considers the number of followers your channel has when ranking your videos in the Subscriptions feed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grow and maintain an engaged subscriber base; bigger follower counts contribute to better visibility in subscribers’ subscription results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subscriber acquisition — genuine asks
rubrics_metrics.description: Be genuine when you ask for subscribers. Users have a better reaction when you explain the benefits of subscribing to your channel and how your channel supports you.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use honest, audience-centered subscription CTAs explaining benefits rather than generic or manipulative prompts.
